trust_decision.summary: Response header names, which may come from the application or user data, are passed to the PSGI header array; headers_to_array strips CR/LF from values only, never from names.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names headers_to_array directly; the value sanitisation is two lines below the loop variable $k.

fix_sites.entry_point: Dancer2::Core::Response->to_psgi (every non-streaming route response, lib/Dancer2/Core/Response.pm:226,243); streaming DSL content/flush (lib/Dancer2/Core/DSL.pm:336-339, 400-402); send_file streaming (lib/Dancer2/Core/App.pm:1244-1246); public method headers_to_array($headers)
fix_sites.module_kind: core response object (single shared PSGI header serialiser)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All header emission at the pinned commit funnels through headers_to_array (lib/Dancer2/Core/Response.pm:226,243; lib/Dancer2/Core/DSL.pm:338,401; lib/Dancer2/Core/App.pm:1245). The only other PSGI header arrays are static literals (lib/Dancer2/Core/App.pm:1593-1597, 1605-1609).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is nothing to dismiss. The one sink is the function named in the report. The only arguable point is whether the name should be sanitised (as the published fix does) or rejected: 'header names come from the developer, not the user'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Value folding (CRLF+LWS collapses to one SP) and multi-valued push_header must keep working. The fix's test expects the sanitised name to be kept ('X-BadInjected: Yes'), not dropped and not croaked on, so a fix that rejects or drops the header breaks the expected behaviour.

O6_input_shapes: CRLF followed by SP/HTAB (folding) in header name, collapsed to one SP
name set via header()/push_header()/constructor headers arrayref coerce (lib/Dancer2/Core/Response.pm:37-44) / new_from_array / new_from_plack, all serialised by the same loop

O7_producer.where: Header store is HTTP::Headers::Fast (lib/Dancer2/Core/Response.pm:33-49); headers_to_array scans it directly (lib/Dancer2/Core/Response.pm:68)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: send_file streaming flattens headers itself (e.g. $res->headers->psgi_flatten_without_sort) instead of calling headers_to_array
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The repo already uses psgi_flatten_without_sort for a similar job (lib/Dancer2/Core/Request.pm:592), and the streaming callback builds its own PSGI triplet; it is in another file from the landing point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the delayed-response content/flush writer builds the header array by hand
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The streaming path writes its own responder triplet in DSL.pm, far from Response.pm, and a maintainer could inline a flatten for speed.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: new_from_plack/new_from_array pass header pairs through a separate normalising helper that rebuilds names
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: These alternative constructors take foreign header shapes (Plack::Response, raw arrayref) and are a natural place for a second conversion routine.

O9_family: HTTP response splitting / header injection (CWE-113), header-name variant

O10_build.toolchain: perl 5 + cpanm/Dist::Zilla deps (Moo, HTTP::Headers::Fast, Plack, Test::More, Test::Fatal)
O10_build.project_tests: t/response.t (header get/set, headers_to_array count at t/response.t:49); the fix adds t/unit/core/response.t, which is absent at the pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate or croak in the header()/push_header() setter, which misses the constructor coerce and new_from_plack routes and drops or rejects a header the expected behaviour keeps.

out_of_scope_notes: The second hunk of ff89ac12 (is_encoded reset in around content, fix.diff:50-68) is an unrelated encoding fix, not part of CWE-113.

Log-line injection: the logger interpolates request header values via %{...}h and the message without stripping CR/LF (lib/Dancer2/Core/Role/Logger.pm:93,123). This is a different property (CWE-117) and was not pursued.
Pre-existing quirk: the LWS character class [\040|\011] also matches '|' (lib/Dancer2/Core/Response.pm:70).
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell); Dancer2 source is probably under 5 MB, which would add tiny_repo, but this is unconfirmed.
Whether HTTP::Headers::Fast itself rejects or canonicalises CR/LF in field names was not read (external dependency); the fix's test at fix.diff:401 implies it keeps them.
present_in_latest not applicable (no latest release given; O8 is empty).
